label: ETP ceramic sludge
source: Ceramic ETP sludge (glaze/frit residue, clay fines from wastewater treatment) — documented cleaner-production audit norms, not a single cited table

label: Cutting & polishing sludge
source: A real, distinct category from ETP sludge: ceramic-tile cutting/grinding/polishing generates its own sludge stream (crushing, cutting, polishing, and water-filtration sludge are documented as separate categories in ceramic-tile waste-recycling literature, e.g. Eco-Compatible Construction Materials Containing Ceramic Sludge and Packaging Glass Cullet, Applied Sciences 2021) — previously folded into ceramic_sludge, split out here since it has a different composition (abrasive fines vs. glaze/frit residue) and reuse path (aggregate/construction-material feedstock vs. body filler)

label: Kiln cooling-zone hot air
source: Zero-tonnage sentinel entry — heat is not a tonnage waste stream but is a real candidate for heat-recovery symbiosis (see interventions.json kiln-whr); kept for matcher completeness

label: Fly ash (body filler)
source: Fly ash substitutes a share of virgin clay/filler in tile bodies — standard cleaner-production practice; max accepted tonnage sized as a fraction of the factory's own annual output

label: Spent solvent (mixed)
source: Spent solvent is the characteristic hazardous liquid waste for dyes/specialty-chemical units — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: Spent catalyst
source: Spent catalysts (from hydrogenation/hydroprocessing and similar reactions common in specialty-chemical manufacturing) are a real, hazardous, well-documented waste category distinct from spent solvent — residual metal/oil content makes them a recovery-still/metal-reclaim candidate rather than plain disposal (see e.g. Recovery of valuable metals from spent hydrodesulfurization catalysts, ScienceDirect; Recycling and Recovery Routes for Spent Hydroprocessing Catalyst Waste, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res.) — share_of_basis and cost are an illustrative modelling estimate consistent with the file's existing convention, not an individually cited ratio

label: Fly ash (boiler by-product)
source: Coal-fired boilers (see PROCESS_FUEL_MIX in generate_synthetic.py) produce fly ash as a real by-product; modelled as a candidate symbiosis output to Ceramics, not a hazardous-waste-inventory line item

label: Low-pressure exhaust steam
source: Zero-tonnage sentinel entry for heat-recovery/steam-reuse symbiosis candidates

label: Solvent for recovery still
source: A specialty-chemical unit with a recovery still can accept another unit's spent solvent of a compatible type — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: ETP textile sludge (bio)
source: Biological ETP sludge (dye/fibre residue) is the characteristic solid waste for dyeing/processing houses — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: ETP lime/salt sludge
source: A real, chemically distinct ETP sludge sub-category from bio sludge — lime and salt (Glauber's salt/sodium sulphate) sludge from softening and reverse-osmosis reject in textile wet-processing effluent treatment, per textile-sludge-management literature (e.g. 'Sustainable approaches in textile dyeing sludge management', Indian Journal of Chemical Technology) — treated separately since it has a different disposal/reuse path (construction-material feedstock) than bio sludge (landfill/co-processing)

label: Fibre / cutting waste
source: Cutting-room and processing fibre waste — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: Recycled fibre feed
source: Processing houses can blend in recycled fibre feed from another unit's cutting waste — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: Furnace slag
source: Furnace slag is the characteristic solid waste for foundry/induction-melt units — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: Spent moulding sand
source: Spent moulding sand from casting operations — documented cleaner-production audit norms

label: Baghouse / grinding dust
source: A real, distinct foundry waste category from slag/sand — fine particulate captured by baghouse/dust-collection systems during melting and grinding operations, per foundry waste-classification literature (e.g. American Foundry Society 'Recycling and Beneficial Use of Foundry Byproducts'; IDEM Foundry Waste Classification Guidelines) — often containing recoverable metal fines, a different reuse path from bulk slag/sand
